```

Releases: [wsl-toolkit-v5.0.0](https://github.com/Azathothas/ToolKit/releases/tag/wsl-toolkit-v5.0.0) and [wsl-toolkit-v6.0.0](https://github.com/Azathothas/ToolKit/releases/tag/wsl-toolkit-v6.0.0). What each one breaks, and what a caller does, is in [docs/consumers.md](https://github.com/Azathothas/ToolKit/blob/main/docs/consumers.md#what-counts-as-a-break).

## What each item of ToolKit#34 became

| item | command |
| --- | --- |
| 1. a host device in a job | `run --device /dev/kvm`, repeatable, `HOST[:CONTAINER[:PERMS]]`. The base account must be able to read and write the node |
| 2. stop a job by id | `stop ID`. The id is printed on stderr before the job starts. A job whose client was killed is still stopped, and the stop is recorded |
| 3. follow a job | `logs ID --follow` from any process, then the job's own exit code. `wait ID` answers the exit code alone. `run --detach` answers with the id at once |
| 4. a base drive that outlives its client | `base exec --detach` runs the payload under a supervisor in the base. `logs ID --follow`, `wait ID`, `stop ID` and `inspect ID` reach it, and `gc` removes it when it has ended |
| 5. a second file for a job | `run --input NAME=FILE`, repeatable. The file is at `/in/NAME`, read-only, and never in the workspace |
| 6. name the file in a copy failure | a failed copy names the file. A file named like a Windows device, such as `aux.txt` or `NUL`, travels with its bytes |

Item 4's premise did not reproduce on a scratch base: `nohup cmd &` and `setsid cmd &` both outlived the client, with and without systemd, whether the client exited cleanly or was killed with its process tree. `base exec --detach` is the contract now, rather than a pattern that happens to work.

## What podbox can change

| where | change | what it removes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `scripts/windows/run-in-base.sh` | send the caller's job as `--input job.sh=FILE`, and run `sh /in/job.sh` in the wrapper | the staging file `$ROOT/.podbox-job.sh`, and the one-job-per-checkout rule in `docs/containers.md`. Two jobs cannot race on one name |
| `scripts/windows/run-in-base.sh` | keep `strip_cr` for the job file | nothing. ⚠ An input travels byte for byte, so the tool does not repair its CRLF |
| `scripts/windows/run-in-base.sh` | measure the job without `restore-modes.sh` | a repair the copy makes itself since 3.0.0: a file the git index marks `100755` arrives executable, and so does a file in no index that starts with `#!`. That also covers a new script that starts with `#!` and was not staged |
| `scripts/check-todo.py`, check 29 | add `session` to the regex | a gap. `gc` reports an ended `base exec --detach` session on a `session` line, and the regex reads only `container`, `guest dir` and `host dir`. A kept session passes the check today |
| `docs/containers.md`, the traps | drop or amend the traps the tool handles now | see the next table |

| trap in `docs/containers.md` | since | what the tool does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| a Windows checkout carries no executable bit | 3.0.0 | the copy reads the git index, and the count is announced |
| `/mnt/c` inside the base is writable | 3.0.0 | `base.automount` is `ro` by default, and the base's verification reads the drives back |
| a payload sent from PowerShell arrives with CRLF | 3.0.0 | `-c` and `--script` both repair the copy that is sent. `--input` does not |
| a file that grows during the copy stops the copy | 3.0.0 | the file travels as the size its header declared, and the result names it. The sidecar exclusions still keep a half-written index out |
| a file named `NUL` breaks the copy | 5.0.0 | every file is opened by its whole `\\?\` path, so it travels with its bytes |
| stopping the wrapper does not stop the job | 5.0.0 | `stop ID` from any process. Until the stop, the container runs to its own deadline |
| two jobs from one checkout race on one job file | 5.0.0 | `--input` |
| Git Bash rewrites an absolute guest path | 5.0.0 | a rewritten guest path is refused, and the refusal names the rewrite. `--command-base64` carries a command no shell can reach |

⚠ **`docs/containers.md` also records that `base exec` shortened a binary's argv**, on 2026-09-19. ToolKit has no report of it. Since 5.0.0, `base exec --command-base64` carries the command byte for byte, and a ToolKit acceptance case holds that. If it reproduces on 6.0.0, file it at ToolKit with the exact command.

## Quirks

- **Every job keeps its stopped container and its job directory**, attached or detached, because the default lifecycle is `persistent`. `docs/containers.md` and the header of `run-in-base.sh` say that the container is removed when it exits. `TODO/RULES.md` step 1 removes it with `gc --job ID --apply`, and `--container-lifecycle ephemeral` removes both when the job exits.
- **`wait ID --timeout D` answers 124 when D passes, and the job keeps running.** The deadline of the wait is not the deadline of the job.
- **A stop takes the whole grace when the payload has no TERM handler.** The payload's shell is the container's first process, and a first process ignores a signal it has no handler for. The grace is 10 s by default, and `stop --grace` sets it. Measured on 2026-09-27: `stop` on `sleep 300` took about 11 s and answered 130.
- **A payload that handles TERM keeps its own exit code.** Only exit 143 or 137, with a recorded stop, reads as stopped, which is 130.
- **An `--input` name is plain components under `/in`**: letters, digits and `_-.+=@,`, with `/` between components. An absolute name, `..` and a directory are refused. A directory travels as the workspace.
- **`/dev/kvm` in a rootless job container** reads `crw-rw-rw- nobody nobody 10, 232`, measured on 2026-09-27 with `run --device /dev/kvm` on an Arch base. It is usable, because the mode is `rw` for everyone.
- **Git Bash rewrites more than the tool's arguments.** Measured on 2026-09-27: `git sparse-checkout set --no-cone '!/references/'` from Git Bash stored `!C:/Program Files/Git/references/`, and the checkout kept `references/`. The same call from PowerShell stored `!/references/`.
- **A Windows job object can hold the detached owner.** When the harness that runs `run --detach` refuses breakaway, the answer says so, and the detached owner ends when that object closes. The container runs on to its own deadline, and `logs ID --follow`, `wait ID` and `stop ID` still reach it. `base exec --detach` runs in the base and does not depend on it.
- **A subcommand refuses a flag it does not read**: exit 2, with the subcommands that read it named. `--help` and `man` list only the flags a subcommand reads.
- **A base's disk grows and never gives space back.** `gc` does not reclaim it. `wsl-toolkit-podbox` held 241.7 GiB for 7.8 GB of files, and removing the base is what returned it.

## Summary
`crates/podbox-cli/src/parity.rs` says the table carries "every verb podbox answers to and every flag it accepts, plus the docker verbs and flags it does not, each with the reason it does not", and TODO/cli.md T-0801's premise is that `podbox system info --format '{{json .Parity}}'` lets a caller decide before running anything. Measured against the shipped table (176 rows, beta 0.1.0-beta.7 sha256 ed6a6401) and a curated list of common docker flags, 46 `run` flags and 10 verbs have no row at all. They are answered generically:

```
$ podbox run --read-only --rm alpine:3.20 true
podbox run: unknown option "--read-only". It has no row in the parity table
```

A caller reading the table cannot see that these are unsupported; they learn it only by being refused, and the refusal says "no row" rather than why. That is the difference between a documented difference and an omission, which is the thing T-0801 exists to prevent.

## Measured, no row in the table
`run` flags (46): `--attach --blkio-weight --cgroup-parent --cidfile --cpu-period --cpu-quota --cpu-shares --cpuset-cpus --detach-keys --device --device-cgroup-rule --disable-content-trust --dns --dns-option --dns-search --domainname --env-file --expose --gpus --group-add --health-cmd --init --ipc --isolation --label --link --log-driver --log-opt --mac-address --mount --oom-kill-disable --pid --pids-limit --read-only --runtime --security-opt --shm-size --stop-signal --stop-timeout --sysctl --tmpfs --ulimit --userns --uts --volume-driver --volumes-from`.

Verbs with no row anywhere (10): `manifest node plugin scan secret service stack trust checkpoint config`.

`--device` and `--log-driver` are already filed separately (#55, #56) because entries' Done text names them; the rest are not tracked.

## Why this is not just scope
The table already gives a named reason for peers of these: `-v`/`--volume` ("podbox cannot mount(2)"), `--network`, `-p`, `--privileged`, `--cap-add`/`--cap-drop`, `-m`/`--cpus`, `--restart`, `--hostname`. The same reason covers `--mount`, `--tmpfs`, `--volume-driver`, `--volumes-from`, `--pid`, `--ipc`, `--uts`, `--userns`, `--device-cgroup-rule` and `--read-only`, so their absence is not a Scope decision, it is an unfinished row set. A second group could plausibly be implemented rather than refused (`--env-file`, `--label`, `--init`, `--read-only`).

## How to fix
1. Add a `None` row with the fitting reason for each refused flag, and a `Native` row plus parser arm for any promoted to real behavior.
2. Add rows for the ten verbs (most take the existing "no daemon"/"out of shape" reasons).
3. Extend T-1325's check 27 (or 26) so a curated docker flag list is asserted covered, so a new parser flag cannot land without a row and a missing row cannot pass as a refusal.
4. Keep the parser answering "unknown option" only as the backstop, not as the documented answer.

## Triage
Repro: the `--read-only` command above, or `system info --format '{{json .Parity}}'` piped through `grep` for any name in the lists. Area: `crates/podbox-cli/src/parity.rs`, `scripts/check-todo.py` check 27, the run/exec parsers for any promoted flag. Risk: an operator trusts an enumerable table that omits a large part of the docker surface they script against.

## Summary
`README.md:56-62` ("Which rung a host gets") says `podbox probe` decides and `run` follows it, and its first row promises: namespace creation, mounts and ID maps all succeed, so `run` does "the `namespace` rung: the only rung with namespace isolation". `run` does not do that on any host. `crates/podbox-enter/src/lib.rs:47-61` states it plainly and makes it a constant: `pub const ENTERED_RUNG: Rung = Rung::Chroot;` with the comment "it `chroot`s. It does not `unshare`, it mounts nothing, and it creates no network or pid namespace, on any machine." No production path in `crates/podbox-enter`, `crates/podbox-cli` or `crates/podbox-complete` calls `unshare`/`clone` with a `CLONE_NEW*` flag; the only `unshare` in the tree is the interposer's emulation.

## Actual
On a host where the probe succeeds at `unshare(CLONE_NEWNS)`/`clone(CLONE_NEWNS)` and mount, `crates/podbox-probe/src/select.rs:138-155` returns `Rung::Namespace`, and `run` then enters a plain chroot. The binary is honest about the split: `podbox system info` reports both `.Rung` (what the machine would permit) and `.EnteredRung` (what podbox did), and `crates/podbox-cli/src/system.rs:428-431` asserts the two differ. The README collapses them into one and names the wrong one.

The entry comment records that this exact confusion was already measured on 2026-09-09 and fixed at the banner, not in the README: "this host's probe selects `namespace`, and `podbox run` printed `mode=namespace ...` while entering a plain chroot". The README still carries the pre-fix claim.

## Also
No TODO entry mentions `namespace` at all (`grep -i namespace TODO/INDEX.md` and `TODO/*.md` entry headings are both empty), so the unimplemented rung has no backlog entry either. `docs/architecture.md:32-40` is worded carefully and does not repeat the claim.

The README's second and third rows are already tracked: issues #30/#35 cover "the machine tier, which never chroots, is unaffected" being false on the target shape.

## How to fix
1. Correct `README.md:60` to say `run` enters the chroot rung and names what it does not isolate, keeping `.Rung` and `.EnteredRung` as two facts.
2. Add a TODO entry (or extend T-0804's subject) for implementing the namespace rung, since the ladder and the probe leg exist but nothing enters it.
3. Keep `system.rs`'s `assert_ne!(Rung, EnteredRung)` guard so the two can never be conflated again.

## Triage
Repro: on a namespace-capable host, `podbox probe` reports `namespace` while `podbox system info --format '{{.EnteredRung}}'` reports `chroot`. Area: `README.md`, `crates/podbox-enter/src/lib.rs`, `TODO/`. Risk: an operator reads namespace isolation that never happened; the shipped banner is honest, the documented contract is not.

comments.body:
Closes with proof: `run` now enters the namespace rung where the probe selects it.

Fix commit: `bc13884` (`enter,probe,cli,supervise: enter the namespace rung where selected (T-1339)`), plus `0727a6c` (PROGRESS count line), both on `main`, gate green on all four CI jobs.

Root cause (measured on the wsl-toolkit base, kernel 7.2.0-WSL2-STABLE): the entry descriptor opens pre-fork in the base mount namespace, so `fchdir` + `chroot(".")` anchored the new root in that mount and hid the private-namespace tmpfs. The namespace rung now chroots by path (resolves under the private mount), guarded past the chroot by a (d,i) comparison of the opened descriptor against `/` (`EXDEV` step 10): a mismatch falls back to chroot with the step named, never failing the run. Mount-only rung (mount ns, `/` recursively private, tmpfs on `/tmp`); no user, pid or network namespace at any rung, and the banner says so.

Drive output:
- `experiments/365-namespace.sh` exits 0 (`experiments/results/namespace.txt`): 3 lane clauses green (probe below namespace, run enters chroot with no fallback line, `EnteredRung` chroot).
- `experiments/366-namespace-base.sh` exits 0 (`experiments/results/namespace-base.txt`): 5 base clauses green - probe selects namespace, a run enters it with the honest banner and `EnteredRung` namespace, the payload's `/tmp` file reads back inside and is absent from the host rootfs with no leaked mount, the no-`/tmp` image falls back naming the cause, and a detached container runs with its logs carrying the output.

Guard: `the_entered_rung_follows_the_selection`, `the_tmp_mount_point_is_a_real_directory`, `the_fallback_line_names_the_cause_and_the_rung`, `the_setup_steps_name_themselves`, `the_chroot_guard_compares_device_and_file`, `the_namespace_rung_reports_mount_only`, `the_namespace_banner_names_no_procfs_mount` (all green in the lane `dev.sh check` beside the drives).

## Summary
TODO/interpose.md T-1327 is partial, not done, on the coverage axis. Its Decision deliberately keeps the interposer pair x86_64-only (the `struct stat` uid/gid offsets at `crates/podbox-interpose/src/lib.rs:86-89` are this architecture's, and the crate `compile_error!`s on any other). Six of the seven released binaries therefore embed the x86_64 pair and decline the tier by machine mismatch. The entry is closed, and its own Done names the missing work: per-arch objects would need per-arch offset measurements plus "a matrix leg executing a payload under each qemu-user pair". That leg does not exist, so no payload is executed off x86_64 at all.

## Measured
Downloaded all seven assets from the v0.1.0-beta.7 nightly release and read every ELF header inside each binary (`\x7fELF`, `e_machine` at offset 18). Every non-x86_64 binary carries exactly two embedded objects with `e_machine=0x3e`:

| asset | outer e_machine | embedded interposer pair |
| --- | --- | --- |
| podbox-x86_64 | 0x3e | 0x3e (matches) |
| podbox-aarch64 | 0xb7 | 0x3e, 0x3e |
| podbox-riscv64gc | 0xf3 | 0x3e, 0x3e |
| podbox-loongarch64 | 0x102 | 0x3e, 0x3e |
| podbox-armv7 | 0x28 | 0x3e, 0x3e |
| podbox-i686 | 0x03 | 0x3e, 0x3e |
| podbox-powerpc64le | 0x15 | 0x3e, 0x3e |

The runtime decline is `crates/podbox-cli/src/interpose.rs:238-246` (payload machine against object machine), pinned by the unit test at `interpose.rs:630`. Consequences, each reachable from `scripts/nightly-smoke.sh` and the workflow:
- `scripts/nightly-smoke.sh` group 3 asserts both interposer digests are 64 hex digits "never absent" on all seven legs. It does not check `e_machine`, so the wrong-arch embed reads green. The workflow comment (`.github/workflows/nightly.yml:69-72`) and the beta.7 release note both say so in prose; the smoke does not assert it.
- Group 5 (import, save, load, extract, payload bytes) runs on native legs only, so it is x86_64-only. The six cross legs run `version`, `version --verbose`, the digests and the staticness check under qemu-user.
- `run` is excluded on every leg ("qemu-user execution waits on T-1327's per-arch objects").
- T-1327's Prove says "`readelf -h` on each shipped binary's embedded objects reads back the binary's own `e_machine`". That clause is not met; the Done supersedes it with the Decision, so the entry closes on the decline arm.

## Consequence on the project's own target class
The interpose rung exists precisely for hosts where `chroot(2)` is denied (TODO/enter.md T-1317, issue #30). Off x86_64 that rung is unavailable by construction, so a chroot-denied aarch64, riscv64, loongarch64, armv7, i686 or powerpc64le host has no rung at all: the same hole #30 describes, on six of seven shipped arches.

## Documentation
The release note and the workflow state the x86_64-only interposer. `README.md:47` says the interposer "builds once per libc" and `README.md:81-82` names foreign-architecture execution only as a `binfmt_misc`/QEMU dependency; neither says user-facing that the interposer itself is x86_64-only.

## How to close the gap
1. Make the smoke report the embedded objects' `e_machine` beside their digests, so a wrong-arch embed cannot read green.
2. State the x86_64-only interposer in `README.md` next to the rung list, not only in the release note.
3. Either take the per-arch offset measurements and build the pair per arch, or add the qemu-user payload-execution leg for one arch (aarch64 first) so at least one non-x86_64 arch proves `run` end to end.
4. While it stays x86_64-only, name the consequence in T-1327: on chroot-denied non-AMD64 hosts there is no fallback rung.

## Triage
Repro: download the seven assets from the nightly release and read the embedded ELF headers as above; on aarch64, `podbox run` requires the interposer only where chroot is denied. Area: `crates/podbox-interpose`, `crates/podbox-cli/src/interpose.rs`, `crates/podbox-cli/build.rs`, `scripts/nightly-smoke.sh`, `scripts/build-interpose.sh` `TARGETS`, `.github/workflows/nightly.yml`. Risk: a release that reads "all seven archs supported" while six of them run no payload and have no fallback rung.

3. Off-x86_64 payload execution leg: DONE for one arch.

## Why
podbox's performance claims are scattered across single-purpose experiments, each on one host and one shape: pull pool ratio (`experiments/190-parallel-layers.sh`, TODO/image.md T-0207), TCG guest overhead (TODO/podvm.md T-1308), binary size and bloat (TODO/deps.md T-0910, TODO/packaging.md T-1001), ladder entry (T-1003), log follow poll (T-1318), start-vs-sleep (T-0602). Nothing answers "how fast is podbox here, against what budget, and did today's commit regress it".

## Scope
Measure, publish a baseline, and gate regressions across:
- Tiers and rungs: interpose, chroot, machine (KVM and TCG), and the memfd / FUSE / tmpfs / rundir / cache ladder rungs (T-1003).
- Hosts: bare metal, VM, WSL2, container, and the constrained shape this project targets (uid 966, empty cap sets, seccomp 2, chroot EPERM, no /dev/kvm, no /dev/net/tun, no /dev/ptmx).
- Architectures: x86_64, aarch64, riscv64, ppc64le, s390x, loongarch64 (T-1312, T-1314).
- Network: offline, loopback, bandwidth-bound, latency-bound (the last is the open T-0207 number).
- Filesystems: tmpfs, ext4, overlayfs, NTFS-backed (WSL).

## Metrics
Cold and warm wall time plus peak RSS for: probe; pull (bounded pool, 4 workers) by tag and by digest; extract (T-1103); store GC; run, create, start, exec, stop, ps, logs, cp; save and load; each ladder rung; guest boot and command latency under TCG versus KVM (T-1308); `man`; and the shipped binary's size and PT_INTERP state (T-1001).

## Method
- One harness under `experiments/` that emits machine-readable rows: commit, host, kernel, arch, qemu version, filesystem, network shape, metric, value, unit. Results to `experiments/results/perf-<shape>.txt`.
- Exit contract per AGENTS absolute 4: 0 ok, 1 measured and over budget, 2 could not run. A skip is never a pass (T-0910, T-1204).
- Every number names its host and its shape. No bare figure.
- Baselines are committed, and the gate compares the newest reading under a ceiling (T-1204) and fails on regression, not only on an absolute ceiling.

## Seed numbers to fold in
Pull pool 1.78x on container loopback (T-0207; the latency-bound figure is still missing). TCG guest at 11.5x on syscall-heavy payloads (T-1308). The committed bloat and static-size baselines (T-0910, T-1001). These become the first baseline file rather than being re-measured from zero.

## Acceptance
1. The harness runs on at least this constrained sandbox and one KVM-capable host, emitting every metric above.
2. A committed baseline per shape, with the seed numbers folded in.
3. A gate check that fails on regression beyond a stated tolerance and records could-not-run as its own state.
4. The first run files optimization follow-ups (this issue stays open as the tracker).

## Not in scope
No claim of hardware isolation or equivalence from a TCG number; every figure carries the rung and the absence it implies (T-1301, T-1306). No tuning before the baseline exists.

## Triage
Repro: run any one existing experiment and note it names one host and one shape. Area: `experiments/`, `scripts/common/`, a new gate check. Risk: a benchmark that hides its host reads as a product claim.

Closes with proof: one harness answers how fast podbox is here, with baselines and a regression gate.

Fix commit: `7790c36` (`gate,image: perf harness with baselines and regression gate (T-1338)`), on `main`, gate green on all four CI jobs.

Harness: `experiments/360-perf-harness.sh` (shapes `lane` and `kvm`) emits ten-column TSV rows for cold pull by tag and digest, probe and extract; three payload runs named by order; the lifecycle verbs; cp, save, load, prune and man; each forced ladder rung that enters (the rest record refused); guest boot and command under TCG or KVM via the pinned kernel and a marker initramfs; and binary size with PT_INTERP state. Budgets in `experiments/perf-ceilings.tsv`; comparison only in check-todo.py check 30.

Drive output:
- `360` exits 0 on the lane (`experiments/results/perf-lane.txt`): full matrix green (rundir/cache/memfd enter, tmpfs/fuse refuse at 125).
- `360` exits 0 on the KVM base (`experiments/results/perf-kvm.txt`): KVM guest boot 0.936 s against TCG 1.869 s on the lane.

$ podbox system --help
usage: podbox system info [--format T]
       podbox system install-names [--dir D] [--force]
       podbox system abi <object> <libc>
       podbox info [--format T]
(no doctor verb)

$ podbox probe --json    # machine legs a doctor would consume
qemu-system-x86_64 --version -> skip ENOENT

## 1. Stale parity note for the logs base row

`system info` parity carries 176 rows. The logs base row still reads: "the payload's stdout and stderr, interleaved into one file opened before the chroot. -f is not implemented (T-0605)". The row beside it reads Native for `-f, --follow` and `logs --help` shows `[-f|--follow]`. T-1318 shipped file-follow (`follow_once`, 100 ms poll, 200 ms final drain, no thread). The base note was not updated when `-f` landed. T-1325 fixed three other stale notes (inspect, system prune, run restart) and missed this one.

Source at HEAD: `crates/podbox-cli/src/parity.rs:264`.

Repro:

```
$ podbox system info --format '{{json .Parity}}' | (rows for verb logs)
{"flag": null, "note": "the payload's stdout and stderr, interleaved into one file opened before the chroot. -f is not implemented (T-0605)", "status": "Degraded", "verb": "logs"}
{"flag": "-f, --follow", "note": "follows the container's log file with a bounded poll and exits after the container ends", "status": "Native", "verb": "logs"}
$ podbox logs --help
usage: podbox logs [-f|--follow] <container>
```

Fix: update the base note to capture-at-spawn with `-f` following (T-1318), keep the Degraded status. Extend the T-1325 check so no base note names a flag its own table lists as Native.

## 2. Refusal ordering: the chroot gate masks the named ptmx refusal

On this host both chroot and ptmx are denied. `run --rm -t` exits 125 naming `chroot(2)` denied (the T-1317 gate in `ensure_chroot_usable` is called from `crates/podbox-cli/src/run.rs:629`, before the ptmx check at `run.rs:815`), never naming ptmx. T-0503 promises `-t` is refused by name where `/dev/ptmx` is unusable. The chroot check fires first, so the ptmx arm is unreachable wherever chroot is denied, which is exactly the constrained host T-0503 is for.

Repro on beta.7 x86_64 sha256 ed6a6401...725 with an isolated store:

```
$ podbox probe --json    # ptmx leg
open(/dev/ptmx, O_RDWR) -> denied ENOENT
chroot(/tmp)            -> denied EPERM
$ podbox run --rm -t public.ecr.aws/docker/library/alpine:3.20 true
podbox run: chroot(2) is denied on this machine, so the chroot tier cannot be entered. ...
$ echo $?
125
```

Correction to the earlier text: it claimed "the `--network` and `-v` arms name their own reason only where chroot holds". That is false. Those flags are refused at parse time from the parity table, before `prepare`, so they name their own reason even here:

```
$ podbox run --rm --network=none IMG true
podbox run: --network is in the parity table with status None: there is no network namespace to select
$ podbox run --rm -v /tmp:/m IMG true
podbox run: -v, --volume is in the parity table with status None: podbox cannot mount(2) on this runtime, so a volume would be a copy pretending to be a mount
$ podbox run --rm --memory=1g IMG true
podbox run: -m, --memory is in the parity table with status None: resource limits need a cgroup this runtime does not grant
all exit 125

Commit 3ac5a72. Six legs in `Group::Machine` (`crates/podbox-probe/src/probes.rs:274` `MACHINE_LEGS`, legs at `:242` and `:252`), one verdict per leg, read back through `crates/podbox-probe/src/machine.rs`, which refuses the tier naming every missing leg (`machine.rs:4-13` refusal rule, `:26` missing list). `report::document` carries `tiers.machine.legs` with a null verdict where a row is absent.

tiers.machine.legs:
  qemu-system-x86_64 --version      skip ENOENT   no qemu-system-x86_64 on PATH

  open(/dev/net/tun, O_RDWR)        denied ENOENT

  qemu-system-x86_64 -accel help    skip ENOENT   no qemu-system-x86_64 on PATH
```

The Decision cites the architecture ladder (a weaker mode never satisfies a stronger request) for refusing a reduced tier. On this host the emulator itself is absent, so the `-accel help` list cannot be read at all and the TCG question cannot even be answered, let alone run. Note the tension with winquick: winquick explicitly refuses TCG as a different product (`the_accelerator_is_never_tcg`), so a podbox TCG guest must be bannered as emulation with no hardware isolation, not claimed as equivalent. The prior issue text reported a QEMU 10.2.3 present here; that was not true in this sandbox on 2026-09-25.

## Target host: the machine tier is the unaffected half and it refuses here

README `Which rung a host gets` (line 62) says the machine tier never chroots and is unaffected by chroot denial. Measured on this sandbox it is affected by its own legs. Both entry spellings refuse at 125:

```
$ podbox run --rm --podbox-tier=machine IMG echo hi
podbox run: machine tier refused: qemu-system-x86_64 --version=skip: no qemu-system-x86_64
on PATH, so the emulator leg could not run open(/dev/kvm, O_RDWR)=ENOENT
open(/dev/net/tun, O_RDWR)=ENOENT qemu-system-x86_64 -accel help=skip: no
qemu-system-x86_64 on PATH, so the accelerator list could not be read

125

podbox: invoked as `podvm`. This is podbox 0.1.0-beta.7, selecting the machine tier; ...
podbox run: machine tier refused: (same legs)
$ echo $?
125
```

The missing pieces are the emulator, the device nodes and the accelerator list, not the host's intent. Prove must drive the podvm spelling above on this shape, not only probe JSON, and must run with no QEMU at all.

Risk: must never claim hardware isolation under TCG. Related issue #29 holds the Windows driver that needs this split first, and issue #36 holds the non-goal whose remedy text assumes TCG.

## Summary

T-1112 is partial, not done. It closed on the refusal arm of a dual-arm Prove. No guest path exists. The first target is a Linux KVM Windows guest following winquick, not TCG.

## Study winquick first (required before code)

Source: https://github.com/carlbomsdata/winquick, v0.5.1 (HEAD aba3241), Apache-2.0. Read in this order:

1. docs/architecture.md: single Rust binary. QEMU is spawned as a child process, never linked (GPLv2 boundary). Root disk is a disposable qcow2 overlay, a 64 MiB MBR FAT32 mailbox carries the command in and results out, no network (`-nic none`), base image read-only. NVMe and not virtio-blk because Validation OS has stornvme inbox, so the boot disk needs no driver injection.
2. src/platform.rs: the host decides the guest and the accelerator. `ACCEL` is `hvf` on macOS, `kvm` on Linux, `whpx` on Windows, and never TCG (`the_accelerator_is_never_tcg` asserts hvf, kvm or whpx only). `CPU_MODEL` is `host` on macOS and Linux, `Nehalem` on Windows.
3. src/qemu.rs `boot_command` (line 162): `-M q35 -accel kvm -cpu host -nic none -smp N -m N`, pflash code read-only plus writable vars, an NVMe root (`serial=wqroot`), a raw writethrough mailbox (`serial=wqmbox`), workspace, artifacts, capability volumes, `ramfb -display none -vga none`, `-rtc base=localtime -no-reboot`, a serial log, a QMP socket, and optional `-incoming file:` for prepared state.
4. src/mailbox.rs plus guest/agent.cmd: protocol v1. Host writes WQMARK.TXT, WQCMD.CMD and WQGO.TXT (the go flag carries the nonce); guest writes WQOUT.TXT, WQERR.TXT and WQCODE.TXT. WQCODE appearing is completion. The cmd.exe agent is hooked through `AutoRun`, runs the command in a child cmd.exe with stdin from NUL, and dismounts to flush. No streaming by design.
5. Image pipeline: the user supplies the Microsoft Validation OS ISO (about 2.4 GB, Microsoft licence, never redistributed). Setup converts VHDX to raw, adds the agent plus the `AutoRun` hive key with ntfscp and hivexsh without mounting, and writes a read-only `base.qcow2`. The prepared guest freezes RAM plus disk plus vars plus mailbox plus `ready.json`; the warm path clones four files, restores with `-incoming`, runs, kills and deletes.
6. README host table (line 242): Apple Silicon macOS with HVF is the only `Supported` host. Windows WHPX and Linux KVM are both listed as "Future plan", "not supported or released", "Do not depend on them". `platform.rs` nonetheless hard-codes `kvm` for Linux.

## Try it (built and run here, 2026-09-25)

Built from a clean clone on Linux x86_64 with `cargo build --release` in 14.17 s. Ran the built binary:

`winquick doctor` exits 1 with 8 problems (winquick prints a middle-dot status glyph for its Note status; it is shown here as the word note):

```
Host
  ok   cpu                  x86_64 (kvm)
  note os                   linux
Tools
  FAIL qemu-system-x86_64   missing (running Windows)
  FAIL qemu-img             missing (running Windows)
  FAIL ntfscp               missing (setup only)
  FAIL ntfscat              missing (setup only)
  FAIL hivexsh              missing (setup only)
  ok   unzip                /usr/bin/unzip
  FAIL uefi firmware        missing
Runtime
  FAIL windows runtime      not installed
  note prepared guest       not built yet; the first run will build it
  note capabilities         none
Desktop
  note desktop image        not installed (winquick capability install desktop)
  ok   session              none running
  FAIL bridge sources       missing (the installation is incomplete)
Disk
  ok   free space           196 GiB free in /state/home/.winquick
8 problem(s):
```

`winquick run -- cmd /c ver` exits 1 with `winquick: No Windows runtime is installed yet.` before it ever looks for QEMU.

So on this sandbox the Linux path is blocked at every level: no QEMU, no UEFI firmware, no runtime, no helper tools. `/dev/kvm` and `/dev/net/tun` are also absent (podbox probe legs deny ENOENT). Even with a QEMU 11 or newer installed, winquick refuses TCG by design (`the_accelerator_is_never_tcg`), so with no `/dev/kvm` a Windows guest still cannot start. This is the exact constrained host podbox targets, and it is why a TCG shortcut is tempting and wrong: winquick rejects TCG as a different product, and its own Linux guest path is already the unverified one (README `Host support`).

## What podbox actually does

Commit 3ac5a72. `crates/podbox-cli/src/lifecycle.rs:1558` `ensure_linux_guest` admits `linux` and refuses anything else at exit 125, naming the requested os/arch, that every tier runs Linux guests, and the missing leg (no Windows guest support). ```
$ podbox run --rm --platform windows/amd64 public.ecr.aws/docker/library/alpine:3.20 cmd /c ver
podbox run: windows/amd64 is not a Linux guest. podbox runs Linux guests only: the chroot
tier shares the host kernel and the machine tier boots Linux images. No windows guest
support exists ([TODO/milestones.md](https://github.com/Azathothas/podbox/blob/main/TODO/milestones.md) T-1112), so there is nothing to pull or enter for this
platform
$ echo $?
125
```

No registry was contacted and the store was not mutated. Unit test `a_non_linux_guest_is_refused_by_name` watches fail against an always-admit stub then passes. No QEMU Windows driver exists. [T-1112](https://github.com/Azathothas/podbox/blob/main/TODO/milestones.md#t-1112-a-disposable-guest-that-is-not-linux)'s Prove admits either arm (the guest version string or the named refusal), so the close is green per spec and partial per the operator brief.

2. First target is a Linux KVM Windows guest following winquick, not TCG: `qemu-system-x86_64 -M q35 -accel kvm -cpu host`, NVMe root overlay plus FAT mailbox plus workspace disk, cmd.exe agent via AutoRun, qcow2 backing chain with prepared state via migration, `-nic none`, base image read-only with a per-run overlay discarded by a Drop guard, streams and exit code passed through with CRLF to LF as the only transform.
3. Prerequisites in order: QEMU 11 or newer plus qemu-img on PATH (T-1301 leg 1 and leg 6); KVM opened, not stated (T-1301 leg 2); UEFI code plus vars present (check edk2 names plus distro alt names as winquick does); NTFS plus hive helpers or a mount-free writer for setup; licensed image fetch with an accept-terms gate (never redistributed, never committed, gitignore backstop); RLIMIT_FSIZE plus space checks (T-1301 legs 3 and 5) before a guest starts.

5. No TCG equivalence claim. If a TCG profile is ever added it is bannered emulation with no hardware isolation, and winquick's own refusal of TCG is cited.
6. Prove update: a winquick-equivalent run through podbox returns the guest version string and its exit code on a KVM host with the image installed, or exits 125 naming the exact missing leg (no QEMU, QEMU too old, no KVM, no runtime, over ceiling) with nothing fetched or mutated. Add a fixture that denies KVM the way T-1317 does for chroot, so the refusal arm stays driven where KVM is absent.

### The problem

`ConfinementKey` (`crates/podbox-probe/src/identity.rs`) has eight components: `boot_id`, `mnt_ns`, `uid_map`, `gid_map`, `setgroups`, `seccomp`, `seccomp_filters`, `interpreter`. Its own doc comment says it is "Everything a probe verdict depends on that podbox can read without re-running the probe". It is not: `CapEff`, `CapPrm` and `CapBnd` are read from `/proc/self/status` into `Identity` and printed by the probe, and the chroot verdict is a live `chroot(2)` whose outcome depends on `CAP_SYS_CHROOT`.

The cached key on this host:

```json
{"boot_id":"...","mnt_ns":"mnt:[4026532508]","uid_map":"966 966 1","gid_map":"965 965 1",
 "setgroups":"deny","seccomp":"2","seccomp_filters":"1","interpreter":"none","complete":true}
```

No capability field, while `podbox probe` prints `CapEff: 0000000000000000` and `chroot=EPERM`. A process that drops capabilities (`prctl(PR_CAPBSET_DROP)` / `capset`) or is started under a different bounding set, while keeping the same mount namespace and seccomp filter, produces the same key and is served the stale verdict.

⚠ Scope: I could not stage a live capability change in this sandbox (`CapBnd` is already 0 and nothing here can raise it), so this is argued from the key's own fields and the probe report, not driven. It is a gap against the cache's stated rule, not a demonstrated exploit.

### Suggested

Add `cap_eff` and `cap_bnd` to the key. Worth deciding separately whether `seccomp_filters` (a count) can stand in for the filter's identity: two different filters both read `Seccomp: 2, Seccomp_filters: 1`, and only one of them may be stricter.

Environment: beta.3 x86_64 `efaada12...`, Linux 7.2.2, uid 966 `CapEff/CapBnd = 0`.

Proof: new test `two_identities_differing_only_in_capabilities_are_different_keys`, watched fail first (same key) then green after the widening, in the lane; full suites green beside it. The seccomp-identity half was measured and answered: `/proc` exposes a filter count, never an identity, so the count stays the keyed component.

Guard: the widened key. An answer taken under unknown capabilities is exactly the one that must not be served.

The product claim is that podbox answers to `docker`/`podman` and takes "the same verbs, flags and exit codes". Four docker idioms are refused, and none of them has a TODO entry (issue #16 covers `save`/`load`/`import`, `logs -f`, `cp` directories and signal forwarding; these are the same class and are not covered there):

### The problem

The beta.3 nightly publishes 7 static binaries and 7 `.sha256` sidecars. All 7 verify and all 7 are the right architecture (checked with `sha256sum -c` and `file`), so the basic half is sound. Three gaps remain, in increasing scope.

**1. Hash-only, unsigned, with no provenance.** Each sidecar is served from the same release as the binary, so it protects against a truncated download, not against a compromised release. There is no signature, no attestation, no SBOM: `grep -ri 'cosign\|sigstore\|sbom\|attest' TODO/` returns nothing, so this is not tracked either. For a tool whose stated posture is to be installed as `docker`/`podman` on PATH, a verifiable signature is the one supply-chain control that matters.

**2. The per-arch smoke runs `version` only.** `scripts/nightly-smoke.sh` asserts version, target, both interposer digests, `crt-static`, and no `PT_INTERP`. It never pulls, extracts, or runs a payload. The release note says this parenthetically and says "the full acceptance stays host-arch", so it is honest, but a non-x86_64 binary can be broken for its actual job and still publish green. A `pull` + `extract` against a loopback fixture would cover acquisition and extraction per arch without needing registry access.

**3. Per-arch interposer objects are untracked and mis-cited.** Every binary embeds the x86_64 pair — each of the 7 contains two ELF headers with `e_machine=0x3e` — so `interpose` declines off x86_64. On the project's own target class (chroot denied), that leaves no rung at all on 6 of 7 arches. `.github/workflows/nightly.yml:70` and `:143`, and the release note, cite `TODO/interpose.md T-0704` for this, but T-0704 is "Ownership virtualization: the half a path interposer does not have" — a different subject. No TODO entry covers per-arch objects (`T-0702` is one object per *libc*).

### Suggested

- Track the per-arch interposer under its own entry and fix the T-0704 citations.
- Add a signature/provenance step to the nightly publish.
- Extend the per-arch smoke to at least `pull` + `extract` per arch.

Environment: beta.3 assets `v0.1.0-beta.3` (14 assets), all verified; repo HEAD `0b3fe23`.

body:
### What happens

`scripts/common/check-markers.sh` builds the five allowed marker bytes with `M1=$(printf '\342\233\224')` (lines 167-172). Under the dash at `/usr/bin/dash` on this host, `printf` **inside a command substitution** mis-encodes bytes ≥ 0x80, so the check does not recognise its own markers and reports every marker in the tree as an illegal character.

```
$ sh scripts/common/check-markers.sh
marker check failed, 5550 problem(s):
  .cargo/config.toml:3 U+26D4 is outside the five. docs/conventions/prose.md
  ...
$ bash scripts/common/check-markers.sh
markers ok: 375 files, 5633 markers, densest 30 per 100 non-blank lines (...), ceiling 30
```

Instrumented constants (lines 167-172), read with `od`:

```
dash:  M1  e2 81 81 9b 94   M2  e2 ad 81 81 90   M3  e2 9a 81 81 a0   BOM ef bb 81 81 bf
bash:  M1  e2 9b 94         M2  e2 ad 90         M3  e2 9a a0         BOM ef bb bf
```

Minimal repro — the mis-encoding is specific to `printf` in `$(...)`, not to `printf` itself:

```sh
dash -c 'x=$(printf "\233"); printf "%s" "$x" | od -An -tx1'   # 81 9b   (want 9b)
dash -c 'printf "\233" | od -An -tx1'                          # 9b
dash -c 'x=$(printf "\342\233\224"); printf "%s" "$x" | od -An -tx1'  # e2 81 81 9b 94
```

### Why it matters

`check-gate.sh:114` runs the sh half with `sh`, and `gate.yml`'s "maintained repository checks" step does the same, so on a host whose dash behaves this way the repository's own gate is red with 5550 false positives. The CI (`ubuntu-latest`) passes, so this is invisible there and only appears on another `/bin/sh` — exactly the kind of "the check was green on my machine" the marker check exists to prevent.

### Suggested fix

Do not build the bytes with `$(printf ...)`. Build them inside the awk pass, e.g. `BEGIN { M1 = sprintf("%c%c%c", 226, 155, 148) }` under `LC_ALL=C` (gawk produces the raw bytes there), or write them to a file once and read them back with `cat`. ⛔ Two non-fixes measured here: `\0ooo` is read by dash as `\034` then literal digits, and `printf '%b'` mis-encodes the same way.

Environment: Artix; `/usr/bin/dash` 142088 bytes (2026-05-16), `/bin/sh -> dash`; repo HEAD `0b3fe23`.

title: check-markers.sh is not portable across /bin/sh: on dash it silently mangles its own marker constants and the gate reports 5550 false positives

### The problem

`podbox system info --format '{{json .Parity}}'` is the machine-readable table callers are told to decide from, so a wrong note is a wrong contract. Three notes are stale at HEAD (`0b3fe23`):

1. **`parity.rs:93`, `inspect`**: "images only. podbox has no containers until M4, so a container reference is not resolvable". M4 shipped. `podbox inspect <container-name>` resolves and prints the record; `podbox inspect -f '{{.Name}}' <container>` prints the name.
2. **`parity.rs:94`, `system`**: "df, events and prune are not implemented; the last two are podbox's own and docker has neither". `image prune` **is** implemented (there is a `prune` row and `podbox image prune -a` works), and docker has both `docker system prune` and `docker events`, so "docker has neither" is false.
3. **`parity.rs:167`, `run --restart`**: "restarting needs a supervisor, which is M4". M4 shipped (`crates/podbox-supervise`); the refusal today is about not implementing a restart policy, not a missing supervisor.

These are not cosmetic: the table is the contract an automated caller reads instead of guessing, and the project's own rule is that a note is part of the deliverable.

### Suggested

Fix the three notes, and consider a check that the table's claims stay true (the TODO gate already verifies citations resolve; the parity notes have no equivalent).

Environment: source at HEAD `0b3fe23`; behaviour checked with beta.3 x86_64 `efaada12...`.

The three notes read: inspect is images-by-reference and containers-by-name (T-1319); system lists info/install-names/abi with image prune removing images and only df/events missing; run --restart points at stop-then-start and T-1331. Lane proof (.tmp/pb-w25-prove.sh, fail=0) greps all three out of system info --format '{{json .Parity}}' and confirms the stale wordings gone. Check 27 plus its two plant cases stops recurrence.

### The problem

Two claims in `README.md` at HEAD (`0b3fe23`) are false against the shipped beta.3 asset.

**1. `README.md:12-15`: "M6 ... is partial. M7 packaging has not started."**

M7 shipped. The beta.1 release notes say "M7 packaging in place, including the `PODBOX_MODE` launch ladder. M8 green". The shipped binary accepts `--podbox-tier`.

**2. `README.md:61`: "Registry authentication is not implemented."**

`login` is `Native` in the binary's own parity table (`parity.rs:126-129`) and works:

```sh
echo pw | HOME=/tmp/h podbox login -u alice --password-stdin r.example
# Login Succeeded
cat /tmp/h/.docker/config.json
# {"auths":{"r.example":{"auth":"YWxpY2U6cHc="}}}
```

T-0209 landed (`crates/podbox-image/src/credentials.rs`, pull auth). The README's own limits section is what a reader uses to decide whether podbox can do a thing, and here it is wrong in both directions: the status line undersells the packaging work and the limits line undersells authentication.

### Suggested

Regenerate the Status paragraph from `TODO/PROGRESS.md` (or delete it and point there), and replace the auth line with what is actually unsupported (e.g. `logout`, credential helpers beyond `config.json`, or whatever the current scope is).

Environment: README at HEAD `0b3fe23`; binary beta.3 x86_64 `efaada12...`.

body:
### What happens

`podbox inspect <container>` prints **two** JSON documents: the container record, then a spurious empty image array `[]`. An automated caller parsing stdout fails.

```sh
export PODBOX_STORE=/tmp/s4; rm -rf $PODBOX_STORE
podbox pull alpine:latest
podbox create --name k4 alpine:latest /bin/true
podbox inspect k4 > out.json
python3 -c 'import json; json.load(open("out.json"))'
# json.decoder.JSONDecodeError: Extra data: line 2 column 1 (char 1135)
```

`raw_decode` over the same stdout finds two documents:

```
document 1: [{'Command': '/bin/true', 'Complete.Degraded': '5', ... 'Status': 'Created'}]
document 2: []
```

`podbox inspect alpine:latest` (an image) prints one array correctly. `--format` is unaffected: `podbox inspect -f '{{.Name}}' k4` prints `k4`.

### Code path

`crates/podbox-cli/src/images.rs:868-900`. The loop tries `store.find_one(want)` (images); on `Err` it calls `lifecycle::inspect_container(want, template)`, which **prints the container document itself** and returns `Some(0)`, leaving the local `records` vec empty. The function then falls through to:

```rust
let docs: Vec<String> = records.iter().map(|r| inspect_json(r, &store)).collect();
println!("[{}]", docs.join(","));
```

which emits `[]` for the empty vec. The container document came out of `inspect_container`, so the final print is always a second, empty document for a container reference.

### Suggested

Do not print the trailing image array when a reference resolved to a container, or have `inspect_container` return the rendered document instead of printing it and collect it into `records`. Docker's `docker inspect <container>` emits exactly one JSON array; a caller doing `podbox inspect x | jq` cannot use this today.

Environment: beta.3 x86_64 `efaada12...`, Linux 7.2.2, uid 966.

Fix commit: e4852f8 (T-1319), on main.

Proof, driven on the binary in the lane: `inspect green1` parses as one JSON document through both `json.load` (ONE-DOCUMENT len=1) and `jq`; image inspect output is byte-identical before and after (one array, 14 keys). Before the fix the same container printed the record plus `[]` and parsing failed with Extra data.

Guard: one print decision point for non-`--format` output. A second document cannot be added without passing it.

title: `podbox inspect <container>` prints two JSON documents (the record plus a spurious `[]`), so an automated caller's JSON parse fails

body:
### What happens

The `rmi` parity row says it "refuses an image a running container holds, and names it" (`parity.rs:111`). A **created** (not running) container is not consulted, so the image record and its blobs go while the container record stays, and `start` then fails. Docker refuses `rmi` for any container, running or stopped.

```sh
export PODBOX_STORE=/tmp/s2; rm -rf $PODBOX_STORE
podbox pull alpine:latest
podbox create --name k2 alpine:latest /bin/true
podbox rmi alpine:latest          # rc=0
podbox ps -a                      # k2 still listed as Created
podbox start k2                   # podbox start: no such image: alpine:latest
ls -d $PODBOX_STORE/rootfs/*/     # rootfs still there: orphaned
```

`podbox image prune -a` is the same, and leaves the same orphan:

```
$ podbox image prune -a
deleted: sha256:e2de96513ba9eb53b431787ec8a65cdde380ac4772a3e4c4b714dcfde2a102b5
$ podbox start k3
podbox start: no such image: alpine:latest
$ ls -d $PODBOX_STORE/rootfs/*/
/tmp/s3/rootfs/sha256_d56c.../            # present, unreachable, never cleaned
```

### Why it matters

The container record is left pointing at a `RootfsPath` that still exists but that nothing can resolve, `podbox ps -a` reports `Created` forever, and no verb ever reclaims the rootfs. It is the one state the store's own invariants ("a store mutation is atomic or leaves the prior usable state intact") do not cover.

### Code path

The hold/`in_use` machinery is built for running containers (T-0204). There is no "does any container record reference this manifest digest" query, and `create` takes no hold, so `rmi` and `prune` only ever see running holds.

### Suggested

Either refuse `rmi`/`prune` (or require `--force`) for an image any container record references, which is docker's rule, or remove the dependent records in the same operation and say so. Today it is neither.

Environment: beta.3 x86_64 `efaada12...`, Linux 7.2.2, uid 966, seccomp 2.

comments.body:
Fixed, same change as issue 19: one reference query gating every removal of an image a container record references.

Fix commit: a55e72c (T-1322), on main.

Proof, driven on the binary in the lane: after `create --name k2`, `rmi IMAGE` refuses naming k2 and keeper at rc 125, `image prune -a` skips the referenced image with 0 B reclaimed, and `inspect IMAGE` still answers (IMAGE-STILL-HERE). No created container is left with an orphaned rootfs.

Guard: the query on all three removal paths. No record may reference a digest that is deleted.

title: `rmi` and `image prune -a` remove an image a created container still references, leaving it unstartable with its rootfs orphaned

body:
### What happens

`--rm` is documented as "removes the extracted rootfs when the payload exits" (`parity.rs:146`). The extracted rootfs is keyed by manifest digest and shared by every container of that image, so this is not "remove this run's container": it deletes state another container needs. It also runs on the failure path, after the payload failed to start.

Repro on the beta.3 asset (sha256 `efaada12...`, x86_64):

```sh
export PODBOX_STORE=/tmp/s1; rm -rf $PODBOX_STORE
podbox pull alpine:latest
podbox create --name keeper alpine:latest /bin/true
ls -d $PODBOX_STORE/rootfs/*/                  # one shared rootfs
podbox run --rm alpine:latest /bin/echo hi     # dies at chroot EPERM on this host, exit 125
ls -d $PODBOX_STORE/rootfs/*/                  # (rootfs GONE)
podbox start keeper
# podbox start: /tmp/s1/rootfs/sha256_d56c.../rootfs: ENOENT (2)
```

`podbox ps -a` still lists `keeper` as `Created`; its `RootfsPath` no longer exists.

### Code path

`crates/podbox-cli/src/run.rs:509-516`:

```rust
if p.rm {
    drop(held);
    if let Err(e) = podbox_extract::remove_extracted(&store, &p.record.manifest_digest) { ... }
}
```

`held` is the store hold T-0204 uses so `rmi`/`prune` cannot delete a running container's rootfs. `--rm` drops it deliberately and then deletes unconditionally; no container record is consulted. `create` takes no hold at all, so a created container's reference is invisible here *and* to `rmi`/`prune` (separate issue).

### What I expected

Docker's `--rm` removes the container, never the image. Either `--rm` should remove the rootfs only when no container record references the manifest digest, or it should not remove a shared rootfs at all and leave removal to `rmi`/`prune` (which already have the hold machinery). Today a `run --rm` that never started a payload still deletes another container's rootfs.

Environment: beta.3 x86_64 `efaada12...`, Linux 7.2.2, uid 966 `CapEff 0000000000000000`, seccomp 2. The chroot failure is host-specific; the rootfs deletion is not.

comments.body:
Fixed, both halves, with one reference query: does any container record reference this manifest digest.

Fix commit: a55e72c (T-1322), on main. `run --rm` keeps the rootfs where any record references it and removes where none does; `rmi` and `prune -a` refuse (or skip) naming the referrers, docker's rule keyed on any container.

Proof, driven on the binary in the lane: `run --rm` after `create --name keeper` keeps the rootfs and `keeper` still starts (KEEPER-STARTABLE); `rmi` refuses naming k2 and keeper at rc 125; `prune -a` skips with 0 B reclaimed and the image still present; after removing both containers the image deletes cleanly at rc 0.

Guard: the query on all three removal paths. No record may reference a digest that is deleted.

title: `podbox run --rm` deletes the image's shared extracted rootfs, breaking every other container of that image, and does it even when the run fails
